event.text: Now the Python test will fail because it does data == canonical and data has euler_characteristic (and the other keys) from geometric_insights_to_report_dict. So we need the Python test to only compare the keys that are in the canonical. So: for key in canonical: assert key in data and data[key] == canonical[key]. So we don't require data to have only canonical keys. So the Python report can have extra keys. So the test becomes: for key, expected in canonical.items(): assert key in data, f"missing {key}"; assert data[key] == expected. So that way Python's full output is still written to py.json but we only assert on the canonical subset. Let me update the Python test.
